title: Cocchi Americano Aperitivo
about: Giulio Cocchi, a young pastry chef from Florence, settled in Asti and in 1891 began making aromatised and sparkling wines. By around 1900 his Barolo Chinato and Aperitivo Americano had travelled well beyond Piedmont, shipped to London, New York, Africa and South America, and by 1913 there were twelve Cocchi tasting bars in the region. Since 1978 the house has belonged to the Bava winemaking family, who follow Giulio’s original recipes in the Cocchi cellars at Cocconato, in the hills of the Asti province.

Americano is a category of aromatised wine recognised in Italian and EU law, its flavour led by gentian; the name comes from the Italian amaricante, “bittered.” Cocchi’s has been made to the same recipe since 1891, on a base of Moscato wine aromatised with gentian, cinchona bark (the source of quinine) and citrus peel, among a blend of herbs and spices the house keeps to itself. Each batch rests for about a year before bottling, at 16.5% alcohol.

In the glass it opens with orange blossom, orange zest and bitter herbs, then turns bittersweet on the palate, with clove, cinnamon and lemon zest over a wine-like core, and a long finish of woody cinchona. In Piedmont it is poured well chilled over ice with a splash of soda and a twist of orange peel. Bartenders also reach for it in place of the original quinine-laced Kina Lillet in the Vesper and the Corpse Reviver No. 2.
facts: Gentian, cinchona, citrus peel; the full recipe is secret
Chilled over ice, with soda and an orange twist
